questions.q: What is the key difference between a summary report and a matrix report?
options: A matrix groups by both rows and columns; a summary groups only by rows
A matrix cannot have subtotals
A summary report can only show one record
A matrix is always displayed as a chart
questions.explain: A matrix adds column groupings, so the data is summarized in two directions like a pivot table.

questions.q: In a matrix showing Close Month down the side and Type across the top, what does each cell contain?
options: The name of the record owner
The summary (such as sum of Amount) for that month and that type
A link to the report folder
The column header text only
questions.explain: Cells show the summarized value where a row group and a column group intersect, for example Sum of Amount for a given month and type.

questions.q: Which T-SQL technique is closest to a matrix report?
options: A recursive CTE
A cursor loop
TRUNCATE TABLE
A pivot using SUM(CASE WHEN ...) grouped by row values
questions.explain: A matrix behaves like a pivot: one output column per column-group value, with aggregates in the cells.

questions.q: Why can a column group with dozens of distinct values cause problems in a matrix?
options: Salesforce blocks any column group with more than one value
It converts the report to tabular
The report becomes very wide and hard to read
It deletes the row groups
questions.explain: Every distinct column value becomes a column, so high-cardinality fields make the report sprawl. Use fields with few values, or bucket them.

questions.q: In most orgs, roughly how many row groups and column groups can a matrix have?
options: Up to two row groups and two column groups
One of each
Up to ten of each
Unlimited row groups, no column groups
questions.explain: Matrix reports typically allow up to two row groupings and two column groupings, though you should check current limits for your release.
